candidates.name: Cathédrale Notre Dame
candidates.content: Built between 1176 and 1439 and with a 142-m tower (the highest cathedral tower in France), the Gothic cathedral is undoubtedly Strasbourg's finest architectural highlight. Check out the astrometric clock inside the cathedral.

candidates.name: Musée Alsacien
candidates.content: This museum features articles from the daily lives of Alsatian peoples from the 13th to 19th centuries: clothing, furniture, toys, tools of artisans and farmers, and religious objects used in Christian, Jewish, and even pagan rite

candidates.name: Musée de l'Oeuvre Notre Dame - Medieval and Renaissance Art
candidates.content: A splendid museum of medieval religious art related to the cathedral.

candidates.name: Palais des Rohan
candidates.content: French-style palace, built after the acquisition of the town by the French (1681). Home to the Museum of Fine Arts, the Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Applied Arts.

candidates.name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
candidates.content: It's recommended also because of the interesting building.

candidates.name: Historical Museum
candidates.content: Museum of Strasbourg's history.

candidates.name: European Parliament
candidates.content: The parliament tends to meet in Brussels more and the arrangement with the parliament moving shop between Brussels and Strasbourg several times a year has been criticized as wasteful of money by EU skeptics and penny-pinchers.

candidates.name: Lalique Museum
candidates.price: €8 adults; €4 children 6-18 and students; children under 6 are free
candidates.hours: Apr-Sep: daily 09:30-18:30; Feb Mar Oct Nov: Tue-Sat 10:00-18:00; Dec: daily 10:00-18:00; closed 25 Dec and January
candidates.content: A very large collection of works by René Lalique, a renowned French glassmaker and jeweller active from the 1880s until his death in 1945. The museum is adjacent to the sole production facility operated by Lalique (the company he

candidates.name: Maison Kammerzell
candidates.content: The intricately carved half-timbered frames decorating the upper floors date from 1589.

candidates.name: Council of Europe's seat
candidates.content: Built in 1977 by Henry Bernard.

candidates.name: Parc de l'Orangerie
candidates.content: A beautiful classical park. It has a small free zoo featuring birds and a few other animals. Also has an excellent playground for young children.

candidates.name: Place de la République
candidates.content: A central crossroad encircled by neoclassical public buildings.

candidates.name: Le Vaisseau
candidates.content: Science center for kids 3-15.

candidates.name: Ponts Couverts
candidates.content: The Ponts Couverts are three bridges dominated by four towers from the 12th and 14th centuries. The bridges got their name from their roofs, which they lost in the 18th century. The towers are the remains of the ancient ramparts.

candidates.name: Barrage Vauban
candidates.content: The Barrage Vauban is a bridge, weir and defensive work erected in the 17th century. At that time, it was known as the Great Lock (grande écluse), although it does not function as a navigation lock in the modern sense of the word.

candidates.name: European Court of Human Rights
candidates.content: Built in 1995 by Richard Rogers

candidates.name: Stockfeld
candidates.content: Garden city built in the early 20th century in the south-east of the Neuhof (southern part of the town). Use bus line #24 to get there.

candidates.name: B-line tramway terminus at Hoenheim
candidates.content: Built in 2001 by the contemporary architect Zaha Hadid.

candidates.name: Les BerThoM
candidates.content: Beer bar near la place Gutenburg. Spacious with an agreeable atmosphere.

candidates.name: Café Bar de l'Odyssée
candidates.content: Bar with an intimate interior. Great place to enjoy a game of backgammon.

candidates.name: Le Frangin
candidates.content: Two doors down from Flam's, it serves a wide range of home-cooked pasta and pizzas at reasonable prices. Offering pizza and pasta main courses, meat dishes and Alsatian beer. The owner is friendly and the food is good, satisfying

candidates.name: Restaurant universitaire La Gallia
candidates.content: The oldest university restaurant in France, in a 19th-century building, built by the Germans (which explains the ceiling decorations). It is the last French university restaurant that is managed by students. Not a culinary triumph

candidates.name: Au Petit Bois Vert
candidates.content: In the Petite France district, serves well-prepared flams and Alsatian specialties in a small room with smiling waiters. The chef usually comes by at the end of the evening. Great terrace during the summer under a big tree on the

candidates.name: Au Dauphin
candidates.content: Try the choucroute aux trois poissons; it is very fresh and a wonderful take on the traditional sauerkraut dish. They also serve the traditional choucroute garnie, with up to seven types of meat, including headcheese.

candidates.name: Au Brasseur
candidates.content: This a restaurant and microbrewery. Try one of their beers and a tarte flambé. Has a small children's menu.

candidates.name: Flam's
candidates.content: Serves a great variety of flams (tartes flambés) and has an amazing winelist for a budget joint.

candidates.name: L'Épicerie
candidates.content: Features sandwiches "tartines". Food from noon to night. Tables on street and inside.

candidates.name: Le Saladin
candidates.content: Tunisian/Algerian couscous and kebabs. No alcohol.

candidates.name: Le Zorba
candidates.content: This little Greek restaurant in the Krutenau area features sandwiches, souvlaki, and kebabs.

candidates.name: Al Boustane
candidates.content: This Lebanese restaurant features sandwiches and kebabs.

candidates.name: Maison Kirn
candidates.content: The restaurant is above a fine Alsatian specialty food shop on the ground floor.

candidates.name: Restaurant Au Sanglier
candidates.content: A small restaurant with a traditional setting. If you want a Baeckoffe, you must inform the restaurant 24 hr before. Mid-range prices.

december.text: Christmas Markets can be found in many places, but the most important and beautiful are fr|place Broglie and fr|place de la Cathédrale, although they are crowded. They are the best places to drink mulled wine (fr|vin chaud) and to eat Christmas cookies (Brädeles).

There are many hotels around the station, especially in the place de la Gare and in the rue du Maire Kuss, but this area does not offer consistent quality for accommodations. Most international hotel chains are represented with the usual 2- or 3-star hotels, many of which host the large tour groups who come on weekend
